---
title: "Compressed rank/select with validated source prefetch"
date: 2026-10-06
format: html
bibliography: ../../bibliography/references.bib
---

The retained implementation is `pixie::RankSelectSupportCompressed<>` in
`include/pixie/rank_select/compressed.h`, with default parameters `<4096,16>`.
It borrows immutable packed source words and owns its metadata. Rank counts a
half-open prefix; select accepts a one-based occurrence rank and returns a
zero-based bit position. The public contract defines empty, disabled-direction
and out-of-range behavior. Serialization is not provided.

## Rank records

Each 16,384-bit superblock has one aligned 64-byte record. Its first word is the
global one count, and the remaining seven words pack 32 local 512-bit prefix
counts in fourteen bits each. Terminal zero/full counts are reconstructed from
the first local prefix. Full-superblock rank metadata costs 3.125% of the source.

Rank reads the relevant record and source basic block. Local select searches
decode the packed prefixes with the retained SIMD primitive, or use the scalar
estimate with exact corrections. The chosen 512-bit select kernel keeps source
words available through word localization. Feature guards and fallbacks remain
inside the primitive headers.

The rank layout stays uniformly packed. Elias--Fano remains useful for monotone
select positions, but its high-bit selection adds work to an isolated rank
lookup. A bulk decode improvement alone does not establish an overall query
improvement; the rank/select decision uses the integrated workload.

## Primary samples and wide intervals

Samples delimit every 4096 occurrences independently for one-select and
zero-select. A coarse sample stores a superblock ID. An interval spanning fewer
than 16 superblocks uses a forward scan of global ranks; wider intervals have
occupied-superblock IDs and relative rank endpoints in a secondary directory.
Endpoint selection uses lower_bound. A bitmap and prefix count map a sample
exactly to its wide entry, without searching sample IDs or reserving a child
pointer for each ordinary sample. Contiguous occupied IDs are derived
arithmetically, and homogeneous directions retain their arithmetic shortcuts.

Dense, nonhomogeneous sources instead store exact selected bit positions in
fixed-stride Elias--Fano groups of 32. A group interleaves the base, unary high
word, optional wide-entry prefix/mask and packed low fields. The maximum low
width is shared across the array, padding every group to one stride. These
positions replace the coarse primary array rather than duplicating it. The
terminal sample is one past the last selected bit.

## Validated prefetch

For exact-position samples, a query always decodes both neighboring positions.
Interpolation estimates the containing 512-bit source block. The implementation
prefetches that block, then checks the target occurrence against rank metadata.
It can correct the estimate by one adjacent basic block. Remaining misses use
the established coarse scan or wide-directory lookup, starting from the already
decoded sample position. Prediction is a hint; exact rank checks determine the
answer.

Intervals wider than 65,536 bits skip prediction. Sources with either population
below `floor(size()/16)` retain coarse samples. Homogeneous directions skip the
position arrays and retain their direct answers. These gates limit speculative
work without assuming uniformly distributed bits within an interval.

## Measurements and reproduction

The current rounded snapshot lives only in
`include/pixie/rank_select/implementations.h`. It retains the measured final
prefetch implementation, baseline and Spider comparison at $2^{34}$ bits.
Earlier kernel/layout variants, experiment runners and their timing histories
were removed during finalization. The snapshot predates code relocation into
the public type; it is not a new measurement after cleanup.

The registered harness compares all nine source families: 12.5%, 50%, 87.5%,
sparse, sparse complement, runs, mixed, mixed complement and FNBP. It retains the
8192-entry shifted query pool and query-only perf control. Optional Pasta and
3-star backends stay behind the comparison build option. Spider is not vendored
or registered because no license was found at the measured revision; its
reported rank1/select1 results came from a temporary wrapper. Compare directions
that each backend actually supports.

Build the relevant benchmark target with the native or comparison preset, list
the requested rows, and run one backend/operation per process for focused
measurements. Set `PIXIE_RANK_SELECT_FIXED_SEED=1` when independently launched
backends must reuse repetition zero. The benchmark's defaults remain distinct
from the snapshot's specified warmup and duration; match those explicitly when
reproducing a timing comparison.

For profiling, use `agentic/cpp/skills/profiling/SKILL.md` and its Pixie example.
Perf text, counters and annotated assembly are the normal analysis tools. Export
the source-aware HTML viewer only when requested. Cycle samples on a consuming
popcount may reflect a preceding load's stall; a flame graph does not isolate
instruction latency or provide a per-query timeline.

Correctness coverage includes the shared rank/select specifications, sample
group edges, low-word crossings, full-width sample values, mixed bitmap lookup,
gaps, partial dirty tails, sampling frequencies through 65,536 and copy/move
behavior. Native and sanitizer fallback checks cover the retained implementation.
